subject: riotInterceptor
pitch:
Category: Vehicle.
Subject: corporate riot-control interceptor with a water cannon and neon light bars.
Style: Cyberpunk 2077.
reasoning:
I'm planning a single TS module for a static vehicle model, no joints needed since it's not a creature rig—using builder calls like part, extrude, and lathe to construct an armored wheeled interceptor roughly 5.2m long, 2.2m wide, and 2.3m tall.

I'm working through wheel placement (six wheels across multiple axles) and setting up box and cylinder helpers for the hull and wheel geometry, with cylinders rotated along the x-axis for proper wheel orientation. I'm also figuring out decal placement—hazard stripes, a corporate logo, and a "RIOT CONTROL" text panel—working out which direction each side plane should face and how that affects whether the text reads correctly from the viewer's perspective.

Writing hull extrusion profile...

Adding a front bull bar with hazard stripes, roof-mounted red/blue neon light bars plus magenta/cyan side strips and cyan underglow, and a rooftop water cannon turret with lathe base, box housing, forward-pointing barrel, hose, and tank positioned above the cab.

For the tank I'm adding horizontal cylinder bands with an "H2O" label, then building wheels with 14-sided tire geometry, rim, hub, and a ring of six lug nuts positioned manually around the axis. I'm also adding dark wheel arch boxes, glowing cyan headlights with red taillights, slatted riot grilles over the side windows, plus antenna, sensors, camera dome, speaker horns, license plate and corp logo textures, and mirrors -- setting overall proportions so the light bar tops out near 2.4 and the turret near 2.7, with wheels at 0.55 radius sitting flush to the ground.

Writing wheel geometry code...

Now for textures, I'm designing SVG decals: a fictional corporate logo like "KANG-TAO SECURITY" with a hexagon in magenta/cyan, side text reading "RIOT SUPPRESSION UNIT 07" with neon stripes, and hazard striping details.

I'm also sketching helper functions for building parts—boxes and decal planes with textures and optional glow—plus a windshield with a dark blue gradient and cyan HUD lines, plate, tank label, and headlight. I'm settling on a hull width of 2.1 units for the body.

Now I'm plotting the hull's cross-sectional profile as a series of (z,y) points to extrude into an armored van shape, slightly beveled, with a sloped hood at the front transitioning into a flat-topped body running the length of the vehicle.

Next I'm placing the cab as a separate extruded profile with a sloped windshield, then positioning a cylindrical tank housing at the rear of the deck and a small turret on the cab roof, working out their z-positions and radii so they fit without overlapping the cab.

I'm also adding a light bar at the front edge of the cab roof made of alternating red/blue glow segments with a dark housing, placed carefully in z and y so it clears the turret, and sketching the windshield plane along the roof's slope.

Now I'm positioning side windows on the cab's x-faces with glass textures and bars, sizing and placing them along the body's length and height.

Then I'm adding mesh grille slats and door seams as thin dark vertical boxes on the hull sides, placing decal text on the lower hull near the rear, and adding thin neon strips running along the sills.

Adding underglow plane and neon strip details...

Now I'm building the front bumper/bull bar as a box with a hazard stripe texture, plus the front grille with cyan slats positioned at the hull's front face.

Still adding parts: headlight glow boxes, hood vents, push-bar rods angled up from the bumper, A-pillar spotlights, roof speakers, antenna rods, and mirror arms with boxes mounted at the sides. Now moving to the rear face design with taillight strips, license plate, and more.

Writing turret geometry...

Adding tank bands, paint colors with countershading, and side label planes. Now I'm planning the roof light bar: a dark housing box with alternating red and blue LED glow segments on top, plus sirens and a rear camera, keeping total scene length moderate.

Working out wheel placement so tires sit exactly on the ground and tandem rear wheels have proper spacing without overlapping, then adding mudguard boxes over each wheel sized to match the hull width.

Adding wheel lug bolts and hazard stripe pattern...
